# dragoman 0.3.8 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dragoman/0.3.8

# dragoman

A web server for scholarly metadata with full [DOI Resolution](https://www.doi.org/the-identifier/resources/factsheets/doi-resolution-documentation) and [DOI content negotiation](https://citation.doi.org/docs.html). Send a DOI as the URL path; receive a redirect to the landing page or metadata in any supported format depending on the `Accept` header.

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- Rust 1.75+ ([rustup.rs](https://rustup.rs))

### Install

```
```
This builds a release binary and installs it to `~/.cargo/bin/dragoman`. Make sure `~/.cargo/bin` is on your `PATH` (the Rust installer adds this automatically).

## Local SQLite database

dragoman can serve metadata directly from a local SQLite database in the [commonmeta](https://commonmeta.org) format, bypassing the live Crossref/DataCite APIs. This dramatically reduces latency and API load for high-traffic deployments.

### Database format

The database is a SQLite3 file with a single `works` table whose columns map one-to-one to the commonmeta v1.0 schema. The `id` column is the canonical DOI URL (e.g. `https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1234`). Complex fields (contributors, references, …) are stored as JSON text.

You can build a database from any commonmeta-supported source using the [commonmeta](https://github.com/front-matter/commonmeta-rs) CLI.

## Running the server

### Start

```
# Default port 3456
# Custom port
# With a local database
# Write a PID file so the process can be stopped later
# All options together
```
Options can also be supplied as environment variables (flags take precedence):

```
PORT=8080 COMMONMETA_DB=/data/commonmeta-2026-06-15.sqlite3 RUST_LOG=dragoman=debug
```
During development you can use `cargo run` in place of the installed binary:

```
# Run from the project root — the sqlite3 file in the root is loaded by filename
# Or with a full path
```
### Error: port already in use

If the chosen port is already in use, the server logs an error and exits:

```
ERROR dragoman: failed to bind  port=3456  error=Address already in use (os error 48)
```
Choose a different port with `--port` or stop the process that holds the port.

### Database file not found

If the resolved database path does not exist, dragoman logs a warning and starts without a local database, falling back to the live API for all requests:

```
WARN dragoman: sqlite file not found, running without local database  path=…
```
To use a local database, place the SQLite file at the platform default path or set `COMMONMETA_DB` to its location.

### Stop

```
# Stop using the default PID file location (/tmp/dragoman.pid)
# Stop using a custom PID file
```
`dragoman stop` sends `SIGTERM` to the running process. The server handles the signal gracefully: it finishes in-flight requests and removes the PID file before exiting. Pressing `Ctrl-C` has the same effect.

## CLI reference

```
dragoman <COMMAND>
Commands:
  start  Start the server (runs in the foreground)
  stop   Stop a running server by sending SIGTERM to its PID file
  help   Print help
dragoman start [OPTIONS]
  -p, --port <PORT>          TCP port to listen on [env: PORT] [default: 3456]
  -d, --db <PATH>            Local commonmeta SQLite3 database [env: COMMONMETA_DB]
      --pid-file <PATH>      Write PID to this file on startup [env: DRAGOMAN_PID_FILE]
dragoman stop [OPTIONS]
      --pid-file <PATH>      PID file to read [env: DRAGOMAN_PID_FILE] [default: /tmp/dragoman.pid]
```
## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `3456` | TCP port to listen on. |
| `COMMONMETA_DB` | (platform default) | Path to a local commonmeta SQLite3 database. Metadata is served from the database before falling back to the live API. If the file does not exist, a warning is logged and the server starts without a local database. Platform defaults: macOS → `~/Library/Application Support/commonmeta/commonmeta.sqlite3`; Linux →`/var/lib/commonmeta/commonmeta.sqlite3`. |
| `DRAGOMAN_PID_FILE` | (none) | Path for the PID file written by `start`and read by`stop`. |
| `RUST_LOG` | `dragoman=info` | Log filter (see ). Use`tracing-subscriber``dragoman=debug`to log per-request cache hits. |

## Usage

### Redirect (HTML / browser)

When the `Accept` header prefers `text/html` or is absent, dragoman redirects to the DOI's landing page:

```
# Follow the redirect
# Inspect the redirect target without following
# https://zenodo.org/record/1089100
```
### Content negotiation

Send an `Accept` header to receive metadata instead of a redirect.

#### Formatted citation

`text/x-bibliography` accepts optional `style=` and `locale=` parameters. Style names come from the [CSL style repository](https://github.com/citation-style-language/styles); locale codes from the [CSL locales repository](https://github.com/citation-style-language/locales).

```
# APA (default)
# Vancouver in French
```
### Query parameter overrides

Use `?format=` instead of an `Accept` header:

```
```
### Format-specific URL prefixes

Two URL prefixes return a fixed format without requiring an `Accept` header or `?format=` parameter:

| Prefix | Output format | Content-Type |
|---|---|---|
| `/dois/{doi}` | DataCite JSON | `application/vnd.datacite.datacite+json` |
| `/works/{doi}` | Crossref JSON | `application/vnd.crossref+json` |

```
```
These routes are equivalent to `/{doi}?format=datacite` and `/{doi}?format=crossref` respectively. The `?source=` override is still accepted if you need to force a specific registration agency.

## Supported formats

| Accept header | `?format=`value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `application/x-bibtex` | `bibtex` | |
| `text/x-bibliography` | `citation` | `style=`and`locale=`params |
| `application/vnd.commonmeta+json` | `commonmeta` | |
| `application/vnd.crossref+json` | `crossref` | |
| `application/vnd.crossref.unixref+xml` | `crossref_xml` | |
| `application/vnd.crossref.unixsd+xml` | `crossref_xml` | alias |
| `application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json` | `csl` | |
| `application/vnd.datacite.datacite+json` | `datacite` | |
| `application/vnd.datacite.datacite+xml` | `datacite_xml` | |
| `application/vnd.inveniordm.v1+json` | `inveniordm` | |
| `application/x-research-info-systems` | `ris` | |
| `application/vnd.schemaorg.ld+json` | `schemaorg` | |
| `text/html`/(absent) | — | 307 redirect to landing page |

## HTTP status codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Metadata returned |
| 307 | Redirect to landing page |
| 404 | DOI not found |
| 406 | Requested content type not supported |
| 502 | Upstream API error |

## Deployment (macOS)

### Installation via Homebrew

dragoman can be installed from the [front-matter Homebrew tap](https://github.com/front-matter/homebrew-tap):

```
```
This builds dragoman from source (requires Rust, installed automatically as a build dependency) and places the binary at `$(brew --prefix)/bin/dragoman`.

#### Place the database

The platform default path on macOS is `~/Library/Application Support/commonmeta/commonmeta.sqlite3`. Place the database there and no further configuration is needed:

```
```
To use a different path, set `COMMONMETA_DB` in the launchd plist or pass `--db` on the command line.

#### Run as a background service (launchd)

```
# Start at login and keep alive
# Check status
# View logs
# Stop the service
```
`brew services start` installs a launchd plist in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` and starts the service immediately. It restarts automatically on crash and at login.

To run as a system-level daemon (starts at boot, not tied to a user login), use `sudo brew services start dragoman`. This installs the plist in `/Library/LaunchDaemons/` instead.

#### Configuration

To change the port or other settings, edit the service environment variables and restart:

```
# Open the generated plist for editing
```
### Manual installation (without Homebrew)

```
# Install Rust if not already installed

### Updating the database

The database file can be replaced while the service is running without restarting. dragoman opens a new read-only SQLite connection per request, so an atomic rename takes effect immediately for new requests while in-flight requests finish against the old file.

Copy the new file to a staging path on the same filesystem, then rename it over the live file:

```
```
If the source database uses WAL mode (has accompanying `-wal`/`-shm` files), produce a clean single-file snapshot first with `VACUUM INTO` before copying:

```
```
### Reverse proxy

#### Caddy (standalone)

[Caddy](https://caddyserver.com) is the recommended reverse proxy for standalone deployments. It handles TLS certificates automatically via Let's Encrypt.

```
  |
  |
 &&
```
Add a site block to `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`:

```
doi.example.com {
    reverse_proxy localhost:3456
}
```
Reload Caddy:

```
```
#### Traefik via Coolify

If the server already runs [Coolify](https://coolify.io), its Traefik instance can route directly to the dragoman systemd service. Add a file-provider config to the Coolify dynamic configuration directory:

```
```
Traefik picks up the file automatically — no reload needed. `host.docker.internal` resolves to the host from inside the Traefik container; dragoman must listen on all interfaces (`0.0.0.0:3456`, which is the default).

# sim_lib_numbers_complex - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-numbers-complex/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_numbers_complex/

## Expand description

The `numbers/complex` domain: complex literals and values, their arithmetic,
and the promotion edges from `i64`, `f64`, and `rational` into the complex
sink of the scalar lattice.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Complex](https://docs.rs/struct.ComplexNumberDomain.html)- Number - Domain
- The complex number domain at the sink of the scalar promotion lattice:
parses `a+bi`literals and accepts the widening edges from`f64`,`i64`, and`rational`.
- [Complex](https://docs.rs/struct.ComplexNumbersLib.html)- Numbers - Lib
- The library that installs the `numbers/complex`domain: its literal class and shapes, the`ComplexValue`class, the complex ops, and the incoming promotion rules from`f64`,`i64`, and`rational`.
- [Complex](https://docs.rs/struct.ComplexValue.html)- Value
- A complex number value: real and imaginary parts over an `f64`base scalar.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [add_](https://docs.rs/fn.add_symbol.html)- symbol
- The `math/add`operator symbol this domain installs a complex rule for.
- [canonical_](https://docs.rs/fn.canonical_complex.html)- complex
- Renders `(real, imag)`parts into the canonical`a+bi`literal form, fixing the imaginary sign and normalizing negative zero via`canonical_f64`
- [canonical_](https://docs.rs/fn.canonical_f64.html)- f64
- Renders an `f64`part for inclusion in a complex literal, normalizing the`-0`rendering to`0`.
- [complex_](https://docs.rs/fn.complex_value.html)- value
- Constructs an opaque `numbers/complex`value from finite real and imaginary parts, erroring when either part is non-finite.
- [complex_](https://docs.rs/fn.complex_value_class_symbol.html)- value_ - class_ - symbol
- The symbol of the `numbers/complex`value class, used to register the class and to tag the read-constructor encoding of complex values.
- [div_](https://docs.rs/fn.div_symbol.html)- symbol
- The `math/div`operator symbol this domain installs a complex rule for.
- [f64_](https://docs.rs/fn.f64_domain.html)- domain
- The `numbers/f64`domain symbol, source of the f64 -> complex promotion edge.
- [i64_](https://docs.rs/fn.i64_domain.html)- domain
- The `numbers/i64`domain symbol, source of the i64 -> complex promotion edge.
- [literal_](https://docs.rs/fn.literal_class_symbol.html)- class_ - symbol
- The symbol of the complex literal class (the `Expr::Number`literal shape in canonical`a+bi`form).
- [literal_](https://docs.rs/fn.literal_instance_shape_symbol.html)- instance_ - shape_ - symbol
- The symbol of the shape matching individual complex literals, derived from
`literal_class_symbol`
- [mul_](https://docs.rs/fn.mul_symbol.html)- symbol
- The `math/mul`operator symbol this domain installs a complex rule for.
- [neg_](https://docs.rs/fn.neg_symbol.html)- symbol
- The `math/neg`operator symbol this domain installs a complex rule for.
- [number_](https://docs.rs/fn.number_domain.html)- domain
- The `numbers/complex`domain symbol shared by this crate’s literals, values, and ops.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_complex_literal.html)- complex_ - literal
- Parses a canonical `a+bi`complex literal into its`(real, imag)`parts, returning`None`when the text is not a well-formed complex literal.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_rational_as_f64.html)- rational_ - as_ - f64
- Parses a `num/den`rational literal to its`f64`value for the rational -> complex promotion, returning`None`on malformed text or a zero denominator.
- [product_](https://docs.rs/fn.product_symbol.html)- symbol
- The `math/product`reduction operator symbol this domain installs a complex rule for.
- [rational_](https://docs.rs/fn.rational_domain.html)- domain
- The `numbers/rational`domain symbol, source of the rational -> complex promotion edge.
- [sub_](https://docs.rs/fn.sub_symbol.html)- symbol
- The `math/sub`operator symbol this domain installs a complex rule for.
- [sum_](https://docs.rs/fn.sum_symbol.html)- symbol
- The `math/sum`reduction operator symbol this domain installs a complex rule for.

# surtgis_relief - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-relief/0.17.0/surtgis_relief/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#surtgis-relief)SurtGIS Relief

Rayshader-style shaded-relief compositing on top of the terrain primitives
that already live in `surtgis-algorithms`. This crate is a *compositor*,
not a new set of algorithms — see `SPEC_SURTGIS_RELIEF.md` in the
repository root for the full design.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-lives-here)What lives here

- `ray_shade`- `surtgis_algorithms::terrain::horizon_angle_map_fast`
- `sphere_shade`- `[0, 1]`, wrapping- `surtgis_algorithms::terrain::hillshade`

[§](https://docs.rs#what-is-re-exported)What is re-exported

Pixel-buffer and PNG output live in
[ surtgis_colormap](https://docs.rs/surtgis-colormap/0.17.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/surtgis_colormap/index.html); we re-export the relevant types
at the crate root for ergonomics.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use surtgis_relief::{ray_shade, sphere_shade, RayShadeParams, SunSample, RgbaImage};
let shadow_mask = ray_shade(&dem, &RayShadeParams::default())?;
let mut img = RgbaImage::from_intensity(&sphere_shade(&dem, Default::default())?);
let shadow_layer = RgbaImage::from_intensity(&shadow_mask);
img.multiply(&shadow_layer, 0.5)?;
img.save_png("relief.png")?;
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Colormap](https://docs.rs/struct.ColormapParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for colormap rendering.
- [RayShade](https://docs.rs/struct.RayShadeParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for `ray_shade`
- [Relief](https://docs.rs/struct.ReliefBuilder.html)- Builder
- Order-preserving accumulator for relief layers.
- [Rgba](https://docs.rs/struct.RgbaImage.html)- Image
- Row-major 8-bit RGBA pixel buffer.
- [SunSample](https://docs.rs/struct.SunSample.html)
- A single sun position.
- [Water](https://docs.rs/struct.WaterParams.html)- Params
- Parameters for `detect_water`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Color](https://docs.rs/enum.ColorScheme.html)- Scheme
- Available color schemes.
- [Encode](https://docs.rs/enum.EncodeError.html)- Error
- Errors produced when building or encoding an `RgbaImage`
- [Relief](https://docs.rs/enum.ReliefError.html)- Error
- Errors produced by the relief crate.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [ambient_](https://docs.rs/fn.ambient_shade.html)- shade
- Compute the ambient-occlusion intensity layer.
- [cast_](https://docs.rs/fn.cast_shadow_ray_mask.html)- shadow_ - ray_ - mask
- Per-cell binary shadow mask: `1.0`= lit,`0.0`= in shadow.
- [detect_](https://docs.rs/fn.detect_water.html)- water
- Detect water bodies as large flat connected components.
- [horizon_](https://docs.rs/fn.horizon_tan_map.html)- tan_ - map
- Per-cell maximum `tan(angle_to_occluder)`along a single azimuth.
- [ray_](https://docs.rs/fn.ray_shade.html)- shade
- Ray-traced cast shadows.
- [rgba_](https://docs.rs/fn.rgba_to_png_bytes.html)- to_ - png_ - bytes
- Encode an arbitrary RGBA byte buffer as PNG. Native target only.
- [save_](https://docs.rs/fn.save_png.html)- png
- Write an RGBA buffer to `path`as a PNG. Native target only.
- [sphere_](https://docs.rs/fn.sphere_shade.html)- shade
- Normal-based hillshade as intensity in `[0, 1]`.
- [water_](https://docs.rs/fn.water_depth.html)- depth
- Compute per-cell water depth from a binary water mask. Returns a
`Raster<f32>`where every water cell holds its 8-connected Chebyshev distance (in cells) to the nearest non-water neighbour. Shore cells → 1.0, deepest centres of large lakes → large values. Non-water cells return 0.0.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)
- `Result`alias scoped to this crate.

# xcm_simulator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xcm-simulator/29.0.0/xcm_simulator/

## Expand description

Test kit to simulate cross-chain message passing and XCM execution.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [paste](https://docs.rs/paste/1.0.15/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/paste/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [dmp](https://docs.rs/dmp/index.html)
- To prevent Out of Memory errors on the `DownwardMessageQueue`, an exponential fee factor (`DeliveryFeeFactor`) is set. The fee factor increments exponentially after the number of messages in the`DownwardMessageQueue`passes a threshold. This threshold is set as:
- [helpers](https://docs.rs/helpers/index.html)
- [mock_](https://docs.rs/mock_message_queue/index.html)- message_ - queue
- Implementation of a simple message queue. Used for sending messages. Simple mock message queue.
- [opaque](https://docs.rs/opaque/index.html)

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [__](https://docs.rs/macro.__impl_ext.html)- impl_ - ext
- Implements the `TestExt`trait for a specified struct.
- [decl_](https://docs.rs/macro.decl_test_network.html)- test_ - network
- Declares a test network that consists of a relay chain and multiple
parachains. Expects a network struct as an argument and implements testing
functionality, `ParachainXcmRouter`and the`RelayChainXcmRouter`. The struct needs to contain the relay chain struct and an indexed list of parachains that are going to be in the network.
- [decl_](https://docs.rs/macro.decl_test_parachain.html)- test_ - parachain
- The macro is implementing the `XcmMessageHandlerT`and`DmpMessageHandlerT`traits for the provided parachain struct. Expects the provided parachain struct to define the XcmpMessageHandler and DmpMessageHandler pallets that contain the message handling logic.
- [decl_](https://docs.rs/macro.decl_test_relay_chain.html)- test_ - relay_ - chain
- The macro is implementing upward message passing(UMP) for the provided relay chain struct. The struct has to provide the XCM configuration for the relay chain.

# cqs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cqs/1.53.0/cqs/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#cqs---code-intelligence-and-rag-for-ai-agents)cqs - Code Intelligence and RAG for AI Agents

Semantic search, call graph analysis, impact tracing, type dependencies, and smart context assembly — all in single tool calls. Local ML embeddings, GPU-accelerated.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- **Semantic search**: Hybrid RRF (keyword + vector) with configurable embedding models (embeddinggemma-300m default; bge-large, bge-large-ft, E5-base, v9-200k, nomic-coderank, qwen3-embedding-4b, qwen3-embedding-8b, and custom ONNX presets). High recall on the curated fixture eval; see README.md#retrieval-quality for current numbers.
- **Call graphs**: Callers, callees, transitive impact, shortest-path tracing between functions
- **Impact analysis**: What breaks if you change X? Callers + affected tests + risk scoring
- **Type dependencies**: Who uses this type? What types does this function use?
- **Smart context assembly**:- `gather`(search + BFS expansion),- `task`(scout + gather + impact + placement),- `scout`(pre-investigation dashboard)
- **Diff review & CI**: Structured risk analysis, dead code detection in diffs, gating pipeline
- **Batch & chat modes**: Persistent session with pipeline syntax (- `search "error" | callers | test-map`)
- **MCP server**: stdio↔daemon bridge exposing 30 read-only tools (plus 4 gated mutation tools) to any MCP-capable client; GPU-free, requires a running daemon
- **Notes with sentiment**: Unified memory system for AI collaborators
- **Multi-language**: 54 languages + L5X/L5K PLC exports, with multi-grammar injection (HTML→JS/CSS, Svelte, Vue, Razor, etc.)
- **Type-aware embeddings**: Full signatures appended to NL descriptions for richer type discrimination
- **Doc comment generation**:- `--improve-docs`stages proposed doc comments as- `.cqs/proposed-docs/*.patch`files for review (- `--apply`writes them directly to source)
- **HyDE query predictions**:- `--hyde-queries`generates synthetic search queries per function for improved recall
- **Training data generation**:- `train-data`command generates fine-tuning triplets from git history
- **GPU acceleration**: CUDA/TensorRT with CPU fallback (CoreML and ROCm scaffolding present, wiring not yet complete)
- **Document conversion**: PDF, HTML, CHM, Web Help → cleaned Markdown (optional- `convert`feature)

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
use cqs::{Embedder, Parser, Store};
use cqs::embedder::ModelConfig;
use cqs::store::SearchFilter;
// Initialize components. `resolve_index_db` honours the slot layout
// (post-#1105: `.cqs/slots/<active>/index.db`) and falls back to the
// pre-migration `.cqs/index.db` path on unmigrated projects.
let parser = Parser::new()?;
let embedder = Embedder::new(ModelConfig::resolve(None, None))?;
let cqs_dir = cqs::resolve_index_dir(std::path::Path::new("."));
let store = Store::open(&cqs::resolve_index_db(&cqs_dir))?;
// Parse and embed a file
let chunks = parser.parse_file(std::path::Path::new("src/main.rs"))?;
let embeddings = embedder.embed_documents(
    &chunks.iter().map(|c| c.content.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>()
)?;
// Search for similar code (hybrid RRF search). #1349: SearchFilter is
// `#[non_exhaustive]`, so external callers construct via `Default` and
// assign fields — adding a new field is a one-line struct edit upstream.
let query_embedding = embedder.embed_query("parse configuration file")?;
let filter = {
    let mut f = SearchFilter::default();
    f.enable_rrf = true;
    f.query_text = "parse configuration file".to_string();
    f
};
let results = store.search_filtered(&query_embedding, &filter, 5, 0.3)?;
```

flexible for arbitrary language-specific patterns without requiring type changes
when adding new conventions. Adding a new naming convention or error handling
style is a single function change in `detect_naming_convention()`or`extract_patterns()`.
- [Onboard](https://docs.rs/struct.OnboardEntry.html)- Entry
- A code entry in the reading list.
- [Onboard](https://docs.rs/struct.OnboardResult.html)- Result
- Result of an onboard analysis — ordered reading list for understanding a concept.
- [Onboard](https://docs.rs/struct.OnboardSummary.html)- Summary
- Summary statistics for the onboard result.
- [Placement](https://docs.rs/struct.PlacementOptions.html)- Options
- Options for customizing placement suggestion behavior.
- [Placement](https://docs.rs/struct.PlacementResult.html)- Result
- Result from placement analysis
- [Project](https://docs.rs/struct.ProjectEntry.html)- Entry
- A registered project
- [Project](https://docs.rs/struct.ProjectRegistry.html)- Registry
- Global registry of indexed cqs projects
- [Related](https://docs.rs/struct.RelatedFunction.html)- Function
- A function related to the target with overlap count.
- [Related](https://docs.rs/struct.RelatedResult.html)- Result
- Result of co-occurrence analysis for a target function.
- [Review](https://docs.rs/struct.ReviewNoteEntry.html)- Note - Entry
- A note relevant to the review.
Named `ReviewNoteEntry`to avoid collision with`note::NoteEntry`(parsed note from TOML) which is a different type.
- [Review](https://docs.rs/struct.ReviewResult.html)- Result
- Result of a comprehensive diff review.

- A changed function with its risk assessment.
- [Risk](https://docs.rs/struct.RiskScore.html)- Score
- Risk assessment for a single function.
- [Risk](https://docs.rs/struct.RiskSummary.html)- Summary
- Aggregated risk counts.
- [Scout](https://docs.rs/struct.ScoutChunk.html)- Chunk
- A chunk in the scout result with hints
- [Scout](https://docs.rs/struct.ScoutOptions.html)- Options
- Options for customizing scout behavior.
- [Scout](https://docs.rs/struct.ScoutResult.html)- Result
- Complete scout result
- [Scout](https://docs.rs/struct.ScoutSummary.html)- Summary
- Summary counts
- [Task](https://docs.rs/struct.TaskResult.html)- Result
- Complete task analysis result.
- [Task](https://docs.rs/struct.TaskSummary.html)- Summary
- Summary statistics for a task result.
- [Test](https://docs.rs/struct.TestEntry.html)- Entry
- Test that exercises the entry point.

- Affected test with call depth
- [Test](https://docs.rs/struct.TestMatch.html)- Match
- A test function that reaches the target through the call graph.
- [Test](https://docs.rs/struct.TestSuggestion.html)- Suggestion
- A suggested test for an untested caller
- [Transitive](https://docs.rs/struct.TransitiveCaller.html)- Caller
- Transitive caller at a given depth
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeImpacted.html)- Impacted
- A function impacted via shared type dependencies (one-hop type expansion).
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeInfo.html)- Info
- Type dependency of the entry point.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_MAX_EXPANDED_NODES.html)- MAX_ - EXPANDED_ - NODES
- Default maximum nodes in BFS expansion to prevent blowup on hub functions.
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_MAX_TEST_SEARCH_DEPTH.html)- MAX_ - TEST_ - SEARCH_ - DEPTH
- Default maximum depth for test search BFS.
Exposed via `max_test_depth`parameters on analysis functions.

- Default callee BFS expansion depth.

- Default minimum search score threshold for placement suggestions.

- Default number of search results for scout.
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_SCOUT_SEARCH_THRESHOLD.html)- SCOUT_ - SEARCH_ - THRESHOLD
- Default minimum search score threshold for scout.
- [EMBEDDING_](https://docs.rs/constant.EMBEDDING_DIM.html)- DIM
- Default embedding dimension, derived from `ModelConfig::default_model().dim`. The actual dimension is detected at runtime from the model output. Use`Embedder::embedding_dim()`for the runtime value.

- Filename of the SQLite index database inside `INDEX_DIR`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [analyze_](https://docs.rs/fn.analyze_diff_impact.html)- diff_ - impact
- Run impact analysis across all changed functions from a diff. Fetches call graph and test chunks once, then analyzes each function. Results are deduplicated by name.
- [analyze_](https://docs.rs/fn.analyze_diff_impact_with_graph.html)- diff_ - impact_ - with_ - graph
- Like `analyze_diff_impact``root`. Use when the caller already has the graph/test_chunks (e.g.,`review_diff`which also needs them for risk scoring).
- [analyze_](https://docs.rs/fn.analyze_diff_impact_with_graph_overlay.html)- diff_ - impact_ - with_ - graph_ - overlay
- Worktree-overlay-aware diff impact (#1858 Part B PR3). Identical to
`analyze_diff_impact_with_graph``overlay`is`None`. When`Some`, ONLY the direct`all_callers`section reflects the worktree delta — parent caller rows whose call-site origin is in`masked_origins`are dropped and the overlay’s caller rows (for the same changed-function names) are unioned, the same single-call mask+union`cqs callers`/`cqs impact`use. The affected-tests section (reverse-BFS over the parent`CallGraph`) stays on parent-truth: a fully-merged call graph is a separate, larger surface, so this overlays the primary “who breaks” signal only. (`review_diff`’s risk scoring reads the same parent graph and likewise stays parent-truth.)
- [analyze_](https://docs.rs/fn.analyze_impact.html)- impact
- Run impact analysis: find callers, affected tests, and transitive callers.
Paths in the returned result are relative to `root`. When`opts.include_types`is true, also performs one-hop type expansion: finds other functions that share type dependencies with the target via`type_edges`.
- [analyze_](https://docs.rs/fn.analyze_impact_overlay.html)- impact_ - overlay
- Worktree-overlay-aware impact analysis (#1858 Part B). Identical to
`analyze_impact``overlay`is`None`. When`Some`, ONLY the direct`callers`section reflects the worktree delta — its parent rows whose call-site origin was edited are masked and the overlay’s caller rows are unioned, the same single-call mask+union`merge_callers`applies to`cqs callers`. The affected-tests and transitive-caller sections (reverse-BFS over the parent`CallGraph`) and the type-impacted section (parent`type_edges`) stay on parent-truth: a fully-merged call graph is a separate, larger surface, so this PR overlays the primary “who breaks” signal only.
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_hints.html)- hints
- Compute caller count and test count for a single function.
Convenience wrapper that loads graph internally. Pass `prefetched_caller_count`to avoid re-querying callers when the caller already has them (e.g.,`explain`fetches callers before this).
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_hints_batch.html)- hints_ - batch
- Batch compute hints for multiple functions using forward BFS.
A single `test_reachability`call covers all functions, instead of N independent`reverse_bfs`calls.
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_hints_with_graph.html)- hints_ - with_ - graph
- Core implementation — accepts pre-loaded graph and test chunks. Use this when processing multiple functions to avoid loading the graph N times (e.g., scout, which processes 10+ functions).
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_risk_and_tests.html)- risk_ - and_ - tests
- Compute risk scores and collect deduplicated tests in a single pass.
Shares BFS results across risk scoring and test collection, avoiding the
duplicate `reverse_bfs`that occurs when calling`compute_risk_batch`and`find_affected_tests_with_chunks`separately.
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_risk_batch.html)- risk_ - batch
- Compute risk scores for a batch of function names.
Uses pre-loaded call graph and test chunks to avoid repeated queries.
Formula: `score = caller_count * (1.0 - test_ratio)`where`test_ratio = min(test_count / max(caller_count, 1), 1.0)`. Entry-point handling: functions with 0 callers and 0 tests get`Medium`risk (likely entry points that should have tests). Uses a single forward BFS from all test nodes to build a reachability map, instead of N independent reverse_bfs calls.
- [diff_](https://docs.rs/fn.diff_impact_empty_json.html)- impact_ - empty_ - json
- Shared empty-diff JSON envelope.
- [diff_](https://docs.rs/fn.diff_impact_to_json.html)- impact_ - to_ - json
- Serialize diff impact result to JSON.
- [duration_](https://docs.rs/fn.duration_to_mtime_millis.html)- to_ - mtime_ - millis
- Convert a `std::time::Duration``i64`for storage in SQLite`INTEGER`mtime columns.
- [enumerate_](https://docs.rs/fn.enumerate_files.html)- files
- Enumerate files to index in a project directory.
- [enumerate_](https://docs.rs/fn.enumerate_files_iter.html)- files_ - iter
- Streaming variant of `enumerate_files``root`, applying the same`.gitignore`/`.cqsignore`/ size-cap / hidden-file filters as the eager wrapper.
- [env_](https://docs.rs/fn.env_falsy.html)- falsy
- Test whether a string is one of the canonical “off” tokens the cqs CLI
accepts in `CQS_*`env vars:`"0"`,`"false"`,`"no"`,`"off"`— case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed.
- [extract_](https://docs.rs/fn.extract_modify_targets.html)- modify_ - targets
- Extract modify target names from scout results.
- [find_](https://docs.rs/fn.find_hotspots.html)- hotspots
- Find the most-called functions in the codebase (hotspots).
Returns [`Hotspot`] entries sorted by caller count descending.
- [find_](https://docs.rs/fn.find_related.html)- related
- Find functions related to `target_name`by co-occurrence. Three dimensions:
- [find_](https://docs.rs/fn.find_test_matches.html)- test_ - matches
- Find test functions that can reach `target_name`through the call graph via reverse BFS, up to`max_depth`hops.
- [format_](https://docs.rs/fn.format_test_suggestions.html)- test_ - suggestions
- Format test suggestions as JSON values.
- [gather](https://docs.rs/fn.gather.html)
- Gather relevant code chunks for a query.
- [gather_](https://docs.rs/fn.gather_cross_index_with_index.html)- cross_ - index_ - with_ - index
- Cross-index gather: seed from a reference index, bridge into project code, BFS expand.
- [gather_](https://docs.rs/fn.gather_max_nodes.html)- max_ - nodes
- Read CQS_GATHER_MAX_NODES once via OnceLock, not on every GatherOptions::default().
- [gather_](https://docs.rs/fn.gather_with_graph.html)- with_ - graph
- Like `gather`
- [gather_](https://docs.rs/fn.gather_with_graph_overlay.html)- with_ - graph_ - overlay
- Like `gather_with_graph``Some`shadows the parent index for the SEED search so a worktree-added/edited file surfaces as a gather seed;`None`is byte- identical to`gather_with_graph`
- [gather_](https://docs.rs/fn.gather_with_overlay.html)- with_ - overlay
- Like `gather``Some`shadows the parent index for the SEED search;`None`is byte-identical to`gather``Some`— see`dispatch_gather`. The BFS expansion stays on parent-truth (the adapter emits a`seed-only``_meta.overlay_graph`marker).
- [generate_](https://docs.rs/fn.generate_nl_description_with_seq_len.html)- nl_ - description_ - with_ - seq_ - len
- Generate natural language description from chunk metadata.
- [generate_](https://docs.rs/fn.generate_nl_with_call_context_and_summary.html)- nl_ - with_ - call_ - context_ - and_ - summary
- Generate NL with call context and optional LLM summary.
- [generate_](https://docs.rs/fn.generate_nl_with_template_and_seq_len.html)- nl_ - with_ - template_ - and_ - seq_ - len
- Generate NL using the active model’s `max_seq_length`from`ModelConfig`. Models with a 512 sequence length behave the same; larger models (nomic-coderank 2048) get a proportionally larger preview budget.
- [impact_](https://docs.rs/fn.impact_to_json.html)- to_ - json
- Serialize impact result to JSON.
- [impact_](https://docs.rs/fn.impact_to_mermaid.html)- to_ - mermaid
- Generate a mermaid diagram from impact result.
- [index_](https://docs.rs/fn.index_notes.html)- notes
- Index notes into the database (store without embeddings)
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_test_chunk.html)- test_ - chunk
- Unified test-chunk detection heuristic.
- [map_](https://docs.rs/fn.map_hunks_to_functions.html)- hunks_ - to_ - functions
- Map diff hunks to function names using the index. For each hunk, finds chunks whose line range overlaps the hunk’s range. Returns deduplicated function names.
- [max_](https://docs.rs/fn.max_file_size.html)- file_ - size
- Resolve the per-file size cap, checking `CQS_MAX_FILE_SIZE`first. Zero falls back to the default — disabling the cap entirely would OOM on multi-GB artifacts.
- [normalize_](https://docs.rs/fn.normalize_for_fts.html)- for_ - fts
- Normalize code text for FTS5 indexing.
Splits identifiers on camelCase/snake_case boundaries and joins with spaces.
Used to make code searchable with natural language queries.
Output is capped (default 16 KiB; override via `CQS_FTS_NORMALIZE_MAX`) to prevent memory issues with pathological inputs. Truncation is surfaced at`WARN`level so silent FTS-recall gaps on long chunks become visible.
- [normalize_](https://docs.rs/fn.normalize_path.html)- path
- Normalize a path to a string with forward slashes.
- [normalize_](https://docs.rs/fn.normalize_slashes.html)- slashes
- Normalize backslashes to forward slashes in a string path.
- [onboard](https://docs.rs/fn.onboard.html)
- Produce a guided tour of a concept in the codebase.
- [panic_](https://docs.rs/fn.panic_message.html)- message
- Extract a human-readable message from a thread panic payload.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_unified_diff.html)- unified_ - diff
- Parse unified diff output into hunks.
Handles standard `git diff`output:
- [rel_](https://docs.rs/fn.rel_display.html)- display
- Relativize a path against a root and normalize separators for display.
- [relativize_](https://docs.rs/fn.relativize_or_warn.html)- or_ - warn
- Relativize `file`against`root`. On case-insensitive filesystems (Windows NTFS, macOS HFS+/APFS default),`path.starts_with(root)`can pass while`path.strip_prefix(root)`byte-equals fails — case skew between the canonicalized project root and the indexed chunk path. Centralizes the “warn-and-fall-back” shim`enumerate_files`also uses, so caller sites don’t silently leak absolute paths into JSON envelopes documented as “relative to project root”.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_index_db.html)- index_ - db
- Resolve the active index.db path within a project’s `.cqs/`dir.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_index_dir.html)- index_ - dir
- Resolve the index directory for a project, migrating from `.cq/`to`.cqs/`if needed.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_slot_dir.html)- slot_ - dir
- Compute the slot directory path: `<project_cqs_dir>/slots/<slot_name>/`.
- [review_](https://docs.rs/fn.review_diff.html)- diff
- Analyze a unified diff and produce a comprehensive review. Steps:
- [review_](https://docs.rs/fn.review_diff_overlay.html)- diff_ - overlay
- Worktree-overlay-aware `review_diff``review_diff``overlay`is`None`. When`Some`, ONLY the`affected_callers`section reflects the worktree delta (via the same mask+union`cqs callers`/`cqs impact`apply, through`crate::impact::analyze_diff_impact_with_graph_overlay``affected_tests`section and the per-function risk scores (`compute_risk_batch`) stay on parent-truth — they read the parent`CallGraph`, a separate, larger surface this PR does not overlay. The notes and staleness sections are parent-truth by nature (they key off the changed FILE paths from the diff, not the call graph).
- [scout](https://docs.rs/fn.scout.html)
- Run scout analysis for a task description.
- [scout_](https://docs.rs/fn.scout_with_options.html)- with_ - options
- Run scout analysis with configurable search parameters.
- [scout_](https://docs.rs/fn.scout_with_overlay.html)- with_ - overlay
- Like `scout_with_options``Some`shadows the parent index for the SEED search so a worktree-added/edited file surfaces as a scout seed;`None`is byte-identical to`scout_with_options``Some`— see`dispatch_scout`.
- [search_](https://docs.rs/fn.search_across_projects.html)- across_ - projects
- Search across all registered projects.
- [semantic_](https://docs.rs/fn.semantic_diff.html)- diff
- Run a semantic diff between two stores.
- [serialize_](https://docs.rs/fn.serialize_path_normalized.html)- path_ - normalized
- Serde serializer for `PathBuf`fields: forward-slash normalized.
- [suggest_](https://docs.rs/fn.suggest_placement.html)- placement
- Suggest where to place new code matching a description.
Uses default search parameters. For custom parameters, use `suggest_placement_with_options`
- [suggest_](https://docs.rs/fn.suggest_placement_with_options.html)- placement_ - with_ - options
- Suggest where to place new code matching a description with configurable search parameters.
If `opts.query_embedding`is set, reuses it (avoids redundant ONNX inference). Otherwise, computes the embedding from`description`using`embedder`.
- [suggest_](https://docs.rs/fn.suggest_tests.html)- tests
- Suggest tests for untested callers in an impact result.
Loads its own call graph and test chunks — only called when `--suggest-tests`is set, so the normal path pays zero overhead.
- [task](https://docs.rs/fn.task.html)
- Produce complete implementation context for a task description.
- [task_](https://docs.rs/fn.task_with_resources.html)- with_ - resources
- Like `task`
- [task_](https://docs.rs/fn.task_with_resources_overlay.html)- with_ - resources_ - overlay
- Like `task_with_resources``Some`shadows the parent index for the scout SEED search;`None`is byte-identical to`task_with_resources``Some`— see`dispatch_task`. The downstream gather/impact/placement phases stay on parent-truth.
- [temp_](https://docs.rs/fn.temp_suffix.html)- suffix
- Generate an unpredictable u64 suffix for temporary file names.
- [tokenize_](https://docs.rs/fn.tokenize_identifier.html)- identifier
- Split identifier on snake_case and camelCase boundaries. Note: This function splits on every uppercase letter, so acronyms like “XMLParser” become individual letters. This is intentional for search tokenization where “xml parser” is more useful than preserving “XML”.
- [unix_](https://docs.rs/fn.unix_secs_i64.html)- secs_ - i64
- Defensive `SystemTime::now() → Unix seconds as i64`.

# surtgis_algorithms - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-algorithms/0.17.0/surtgis_algorithms/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#surtgis-algorithms)SurtGis Algorithms

Geospatial analysis algorithms for SurtGis.

[§](https://docs.rs#available-algorithm-categories)Available Algorithm Categories

- **terrain**: Slope, aspect, hillshade, curvature, TPI, TRI, landform, TWI, SPI, STI, geomorphons, viewshed, SVF, openness, convergence, multiscale curvatures, feature-preserving smoothing, wind exposure, solar radiation, MRVBF/MRRTF, northness/eastness, DEV, multidirectional hillshade, shape index, curvedness, log transform, accumulation zones
- **hydrology**: Fill sinks, Priority-Flood, flow direction, flow accumulation, watershed, HAND, stream network
- **imagery**: Spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, NDRE, GNDVI, NGRDI, RECI, etc.), band math, reclassification
- **interpolation**: IDW, nearest neighbor, TIN
- **vector**: Buffer, simplify, spatial operations, clipping, measurements
- **morphology**: Erosion, dilation, opening, closing, gradient, top-hat, black-hat
- **statistics**: Focal statistics, zonal statistics, spatial autocorrelation

# derive_more 2.1.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/derive_more/2.1.1

`derive_more`

Rust has lots of builtin traits that are implemented for its basic types, such
as `Add`, `Not`, `From` or `Display`.
However, when wrapping these types inside your own structs or enums you lose the
implementations of these traits and are required to recreate them.
This is especially annoying when your own structures are very simple, such as
when using the commonly advised newtype pattern (e.g. `MyInt(i32)`).

This library tries to remove these annoyances and the corresponding boilerplate code. It does this by allowing you to derive lots of commonly used traits for both structs and enums.

## Example code

By using this library the following code just works:

```
use ;
;
assert!;
assert!;
assert!;
assert!;
assert!;
assert!;
```
## The derivable traits

Below are all the traits that you can derive using this library. Some trait derivations are so similar that the further documentation will only show a single one of them. You can recognize these by the "-like" suffix in their name. The trait name before that will be the only one that is used throughout the further documentation.

It is important to understand what code gets generated when using one of the derives from this crate. That is why the links below explain what code gets generated for a trait for each group from before.

You can use the [ cargo-expand](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-expand) utility to see the exact code that is generated
for your specific type.
This will show you your code with all macros and derives expanded.

**NOTE**: You still have to derive each trait separately. So `#[derive(Mul)]` doesn't
automatically derive `Div` as well. To derive both you should do `#[derive(Mul, Div)]`

### Conversion traits

These are traits that are used to convert automatically between types.

### Formatting traits

These traits are used for converting a struct to a string in different ways.

- `Debug`
- `Display`-like- `Display`,- `Binary`,- `Octal`,- `LowerHex`,- `UpperHex`,- `LowerExp`,- `UpperExp`,- `Pointer`

### Error-handling traits

These traits are used to define error-types.

### Operators

These are traits that can be used for operator overloading.

- `Index`
- `Deref`
- `Not`-like- `Not`and- `Neg`
- `Add`-like- `Add`,- `Sub`,- `BitAnd`,- `BitOr`,- `BitXor`
- `Mul`-like- `Mul`,- `Div`,- `Rem`,- `Shr`and- `Shl`
- `Sum`-like- `Sum`and- `Product`
- `IndexMut`
- `DerefMut`
- `AddAssign`-like- `AddAssign`,- `SubAssign`,- `BitAndAssign`,- `BitOrAssign`and- `BitXorAssign`
- `MulAssign`-like- `MulAssign`,- `DivAssign`,- `RemAssign`,- `ShrAssign`and- `ShlAssign`
- `Eq`- `PartialEq`

### Static methods

These don't derive traits, but derive static methods instead.

- `Constructor`- `new`method that can be used as a constructor. This is very basic if you need more customization for your constructor, check out the- `derive-new`
- `IsVariant`- `foo`of an enum type, derives a- `is_foo`method.
- `Unwrap`- `foo`of an enum type, derives an- `unwrap_foo`method.
- `TryUnwrap`- `foo`of an enum type, derives an- `try_unwrap_foo`method.

### Re-exports

This crate also re-exports all the standard library traits, that it adds derives
for, in the `with_trait` module. So, both the `Display` derive and the `Display`
trait will be in scope when you add the following code:

```
use Display; // also imports `core::fmt::Display`
```
By default, derive macros only, without the corresponding traits, are imported from
the crate's root (or from the `derive` module):

```
use Display;   // imports macro only
use *; // imports all macros only
```
#### Hygiene

For hygiene purposes, macros use `derive_more::*` absolute paths in their expansions.
This might introduce a trouble, if you want to re-export `derive_more` macros in your
own crate without using the `derive_more` as a direct dependency in downstream crates:

```
use Display; // re-exported in `my_lib` crate
 // error: could not find `derive_more` in the list of imported crates
;
```
In such case, you should re-export the `derive_more` module too:

```
use ; // re-exported in `my_lib` crate
 // works fine now!
;
```
## Installation

To avoid redundant compilation times, by default no derives are supported.
You have to enable each type of derive as a feature in `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
# You can specify the types of derives that you need for less time spent
# compiling. For the full list of features see this crate its `Cargo.toml`.
 = {  = "2",  = ["from", "add", "into_iterator"] }
```
```
[]
# If you don't care much about compilation times and simply want to have
# support for all the possible derives, you can use the "full" feature.
 = {  = "2",  = ["full"] }
```
```
[]
# If you run in a `no_std` environment you should disable the default features,
# because the only default feature is the "std" feature.
# NOTE: You can combine this with "full" feature to get support for all the
#       possible derives in a `no_std` environment.
 = {  = "2",  = false }
```
And this to the top of your Rust file:

```
// use the derives that you want in the file
use ;
```
If you're still using Rust 2015, add this instead:

```
extern crate core;
extern crate derive_more;
#  // omit wrapping statements above into `main()` in tests
```
[MSRV](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-rust-version-field) policy

This library requires Rust 1.81 or higher.

Changing [MSRV](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-rust-version-field) (minimum supported Rust version) of this crate is treated as a **minor version change** in terms of [Semantic Versioning](http://semver.org).

- So, if [MSRV](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-rust-version-field)changes are**NOT concerning**for your project, just use the default[caret requirement](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html#caret-requirements):`[] = "2" # or "2.1", or "^2.1"`
- However, if [MSRV](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-rust-version-field)changes are concerning for your project, then use the[tilde requirement](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html#tilde-requirements)to**pin to a specific minor version**:`[] = "~2.1" # or "~2.1.1"`

# derive_more - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/derive_more/2.1.1/target-redirect/derive_more/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#derive_more)`derive_more`

Rust has lots of builtin traits that are implemented for its basic types, such
as `Add`, `Not`, `From` or `Display`.
However, when wrapping these types inside your own structs or enums you lose the
implementations of these traits and are required to recreate them.
This is especially annoying when your own structures are very simple, such as
when using the commonly advised newtype pattern (e.g. `MyInt(i32)`).

This library tries to remove these annoyances and the corresponding boilerplate code. It does this by allowing you to derive lots of commonly used traits for both structs and enums.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-code)Example code

By using this library the following code just works:

```
use derive_more::{Add, Display, From, Into};
#[derive(PartialEq, From, Add)]
struct MyInt(i32);
#[derive(PartialEq, From, Into)]
struct Point2D {
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
}
#[derive(PartialEq, From, Add, Display)]
enum MyEnum {
    #[display("int: {_0}")]
    Int(i32),
    Uint(u32),
    #[display("nothing")]
    Nothing,
}
assert!(MyInt(11) == MyInt(5) + 6.into());
assert!((5, 6) == Point2D { x: 5, y: 6 }.into());
assert!(MyEnum::Int(15) == (MyEnum::Int(8) + 7.into()).unwrap());
assert!(MyEnum::Int(15).to_string() == "int: 15");
assert!(MyEnum::Uint(42).to_string() == "42");
assert!(MyEnum::Nothing.to_string() == "nothing");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#the-derivable-traits)The derivable traits

Below are all the traits that you can derive using this library. Some trait derivations are so similar that the further documentation will only show a single one of them. You can recognize these by the “-like” suffix in their name. The trait name before that will be the only one that is used throughout the further documentation.

It is important to understand what code gets generated when using one of the derives from this crate. That is why the links below explain what code gets generated for a trait for each group from before.

You can use the [ cargo-expand](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-expand) utility to see the exact code that is generated
for your specific type.
This will show you your code with all macros and derives expanded.

**NOTE**: You still have to derive each trait separately. So `#[derive(Mul)]` doesn’t
automatically derive `Div` as well. To derive both you should do `#[derive(Mul, Div)]`

[§](https://docs.rs#conversion-traits)Conversion traits

These are traits that are used to convert automatically between types.

[§](https://docs.rs#formatting-traits)Formatting traits

These traits are used for converting a struct to a string in different ways.

- `Debug`
- `Display`-like- `Display`,- `Binary`,- `Octal`,- `LowerHex`,- `UpperHex`,- `LowerExp`,- `UpperExp`,- `Pointer`

[§](https://docs.rs#error-handling-traits)Error-handling traits

These traits are used to define error-types.

[§](https://docs.rs#operators)Operators

These are traits that can be used for operator overloading.

- `Index`
- `Deref`
- `Not`-like- `Not`and- `Neg`
- `Add`-like- `Add`,- `Sub`,- `BitAnd`,- `BitOr`,- `BitXor`
- `Mul`-like- `Mul`,- `Div`,- `Rem`,- `Shr`and- `Shl`
- `Sum`-like- `Sum`and- `Product`
- `IndexMut`
- `DerefMut`
- `AddAssign`-like- `AddAssign`,- `SubAssign`,- `BitAndAssign`,- `BitOrAssign`and- `BitXorAssign`
- `MulAssign`-like- `MulAssign`,- `DivAssign`,- `RemAssign`,- `ShrAssign`and- `ShlAssign`
- `Eq`- `PartialEq`

[§](https://docs.rs#static-methods)Static methods

These don’t derive traits, but derive static methods instead.

- `Constructor`- `new`method that can be used as a constructor. This is very basic if you need more customization for your constructor, check out the- `derive-new`
- `IsVariant`- `foo`of an enum type, derives a- `is_foo`method.
- `Unwrap`- `foo`of an enum type, derives an- `unwrap_foo`method.
- `TryUnwrap`- `foo`of an enum type, derives an- `try_unwrap_foo`method.

[§](https://docs.rs#re-exports)Re-exports

This crate also re-exports all the standard library traits, that it adds derives
for, in the `with_trait` module. So, both the `Display` derive and the `Display`
trait will be in scope when you add the following code:

`use derive_more::with_trait::Display; // also imports `core::fmt::Display``By default, derive macros only, without the corresponding traits, are imported from
the crate’s root (or from the `derive` module):

```
use derive_more::Display;   // imports macro only
use derive_more::derive::*; // imports all macros only
```
[§](https://docs.rs#hygiene)Hygiene

For hygiene purposes, macros use `derive_more::*` absolute paths in their expansions.
This might introduce a trouble, if you want to re-export `derive_more` macros in your
own crate without using the `derive_more` as a direct dependency in downstream crates:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use my_lib::Display; // re-exported in `my_lib` crate
#[derive(Display)] // error: could not find `derive_more` in the list of imported crates
struct MyInt(i32);
```
In such case, you should re-export the `derive_more` module too:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use my_lib::{derive_more, Display}; // re-exported in `my_lib` crate
#[derive(Display)] // works fine now!
struct MyInt(i32);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#installation)Installation

To avoid redundant compilation times, by default no derives are supported.
You have to enable each type of derive as a feature in `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies]
# You can specify the types of derives that you need for less time spent
# compiling. For the full list of features see this crate its `Cargo.toml`.
derive_more = { version = "2", features = ["from", "add", "into_iterator"] }
```
```
[dependencies]
# If you don't care much about compilation times and simply want to have
# support for all the possible derives, you can use the "full" feature.
derive_more = { version = "2", features = ["full"] }
```
```
[dependencies]
# If you run in a `no_std` environment you should disable the default features,
# because the only default feature is the "std" feature.
# NOTE: You can combine this with "full" feature to get support for all the
#       possible derives in a `no_std` environment.
derive_more = { version = "2", default-features = false }
```
And this to the top of your Rust file:

```
// use the derives that you want in the file
use derive_more::{Add, Display, From};
```
If you’re still using Rust 2015, add this instead:

This library requires Rust 1.81 or higher.

Changing [MSRV](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-rust-version-field) (minimum supported Rust version) of this crate is treated as a **minor version change** in terms of [Semantic Versioning](http://semver.org).

- So, if [MSRV](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-rust-version-field)changes are**NOT concerning**for your project, just use the default[caret requirement](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html#caret-requirements):`[dependencies] derive_more = "2" # or "2.1", or "^2.1"`
- However, if [MSRV](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-rust-version-field)changes are concerning for your project, then use the[tilde requirement](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html#tilde-requirements)to**pin to a specific minor version**:`[dependencies] derive_more = "~2.1" # or "~2.1.1"`

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- Module containing derive definitions only, without their corresponding traits.

- Module containing derive definitions with their corresponding traits along.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [From](https://docs.rs/struct.FromStrError.html)- StrError - `from_str`
- Error of parsing an enum value its string representation.
- [TryFrom](https://docs.rs/struct.TryFromReprError.html)- Repr - Error - `try_from`and (- `try_from`or- `try_into`)
- Error returned by the derived `TryFrom`
- [TryInto](https://docs.rs/struct.TryIntoError.html)- Error - `try_into`and (- `try_from`or- `try_into`)
- Error returned by the derived `TryInto`
- [TryUnwrap](https://docs.rs/struct.TryUnwrapError.html)- Error - `try_unwrap`
- Error returned by the derived `TryUnwrap`
- [Unit](https://docs.rs/struct.UnitError.html)- Error - `add`or- `mul`or- `not`
- Error returned by the derived implementations when an arithmetic or logic operation is invoked on a unit-like variant of an enum.
- [Wrong](https://docs.rs/struct.WrongVariantError.html)- Variant - Error - `add`or- `mul`
- Error returned by the derived implementations when an arithmetic or logic operation is invoked on mismatched enum variants.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Binary](https://docs.rs/enum.BinaryError.html)- Error - `add`or- `mul`
- Possible errors returned by the derived implementations of binary arithmetic or logic operations.

# derive_more - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/derive_more/2.1.1/derive_more/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#derive_more)`derive_more`

Rust has lots of builtin traits that are implemented for its basic types, such
as `Add`, `Not`, `From` or `Display`.
However, when wrapping these types inside your own structs or enums you lose the
implementations of these traits and are required to recreate them.
This is especially annoying when your own structures are very simple, such as
when using the commonly advised newtype pattern (e.g. `MyInt(i32)`).

This library tries to remove these annoyances and the corresponding boilerplate code. It does this by allowing you to derive lots of commonly used traits for both structs and enums.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-code)Example code

By using this library the following code just works:

```
use derive_more::{Add, Display, From, Into};
#[derive(PartialEq, From, Add)]
struct MyInt(i32);
#[derive(PartialEq, From, Into)]
struct Point2D {
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
}
#[derive(PartialEq, From, Add, Display)]
enum MyEnum {

    Int(i32),
    Uint(u32),
    #[display("nothing")]

assert!(MyInt(11) == MyInt(5) + 6.into());

```
[dependencies]
# If you don't care much about compilation times and simply want to have
# support for all the possible derives, you can use the "full" feature.
derive_more = { version = "2", features = ["full"] }
```
```
[dependencies]
# If you run in a `no_std` environment you should disable the default features,
# because the only default feature is the "std" feature.
# NOTE: You can combine this with "full" feature to get support for all the
#       possible derives in a `no_std` environment.
derive_more = { version = "2", default-features = false }
```
And this to the top of your Rust file:

```
// use the derives that you want in the file
use derive_more::{Add, Display, From};
```
If you’re still using Rust 2015, add this instead:

This library requires Rust 1.81 or higher.

Changing [MSRV](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-rust-version-field) (minimum supported Rust version) of this crate is treated as a **minor version change** in terms of [Semantic Versioning](http://semver.org).

- So, if [MSRV](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-rust-version-field)changes are**NOT concerning**for your project, just use the default[caret requirement](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html#caret-requirements):`[dependencies] derive_more = "2" # or "2.1", or "^2.1"`
- However, if [MSRV](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-rust-version-field)changes are concerning for your project, then use the[tilde requirement](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html#tilde-requirements)to**pin to a specific minor version**:`[dependencies] derive_more = "~2.1" # or "~2.1.1"`

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [derive](https://docs.rs/derive/index.html)
- Module containing derive definitions only, without their corresponding traits.
- [with_](https://docs.rs/with_trait/index.html)- trait
- Module containing derive definitions with their corresponding traits along.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [From](https://docs.rs/struct.FromStrError.html)- StrError - `from_str`
- Error of parsing an enum value its string representation.
- [TryFrom](https://docs.rs/struct.TryFromReprError.html)- Repr - Error - `try_from`and (- `try_from`or- `try_into`)
- Error returned by the derived `TryFrom`
- [TryInto](https://docs.rs/struct.TryIntoError.html)- Error - `try_into`and (- `try_from`or- `try_into`)
- Error returned by the derived `TryInto`
- [TryUnwrap](https://docs.rs/struct.TryUnwrapError.html)- Error - `try_unwrap`
- Error returned by the derived `TryUnwrap`
- [Unit](https://docs.rs/struct.UnitError.html)- Error - `add`or- `mul`or- `not`
- Error returned by the derived implementations when an arithmetic or logic operation is invoked on a unit-like variant of an enum.
- [Wrong](https://docs.rs/struct.WrongVariantError.html)- Variant - Error - `add`or- `mul`
- Error returned by the derived implementations when an arithmetic or logic operation is invoked on mismatched enum variants.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Binary](https://docs.rs/enum.BinaryError.html)- Error - `add`or- `mul`
- Possible errors returned by the derived implementations of binary arithmetic or logic operations.
